choices.text: They are only similar, not congruent

questions.explanation: Scene s1: all three sides of P match all three sides of Q (6 with 6, 8 with 8, 10 with 10), so the triangles are congruent by SSS.
questions.prompt: Triangle P has sides 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm. Triangle Q has sides 8 cm, 10 cm and 6 cm. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: Yes, because their areas are equal
No, because their sides and angles do not all match
Yes, because their perimeters are equal
No, because a rectangle can never match a square in area

questions.explanation: The trap is: Two shapes with the same area are congruent. Equal area says nothing about shape: the rectangle's sides are 9 and 4 while the square's are 6 and 6, so the shapes are not congruent.
questions.misconception: Two shapes with the same area are congruent.
questions.prompt: Rectangle A measures 9 cm by 4 cm and square B measures 6 cm by 6 cm. Both have area 36 cm². Are the two shapes congruent?

questions.explanation: Scene s3: areas scale by the square of the length ratio, 3² = 9, so the larger area is 9 × 5 = 45 cm².
questions.prompt: Two similar triangles have matching sides in the ratio 1 : 3. The smaller triangle has area 5 cm². Find the area of the larger triangle.

questions.answer: 90 degrees, by the angle in a semicircle theorem.
questions.explanation: Scene s4: an angle in a semicircle is a right angle, so angle ACB standing on diameter AB is 90°.
questions.prompt: AB is a diameter of a circle and C is a point on the circle. State the size of angle ACB and name the theorem used.

questions.explanation: Scene s5: the centre angle is twice the circumference angle on the same chord, so the circumference angle is 130° / 2 = 65°.
questions.prompt: The angle at the centre of a circle is 130°. What is the angle at the circumference standing on the same chord?
